title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a proposed law that would set up a national framework for tracking and evaluating artificial intelligence technologies throughout the country. It aims to boost transparency, safety, and accountability by ensuring AI systems comply with national standards and priorities.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 sets out a framework to regulate artificial intelligence, requiring developers to conduct safety assessments, disclose how models are trained, and ensure systems are transparent and accountable. It also establishes enforcement mechanisms, defines high‑risk AI categories, and sets standards for data use, bias mitigation, and user protection.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This law aims to foster the growth of artificial intelligence by encouraging the development and retention of skilled AI professionals. It proposes measures such as scholarships, research grants, and streamlined visa processes to attract global AI talent to the country.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill proposes creating a system that delivers detailed component lists, or functional bills of materials, for artificial intelligence technologies to promote transparency and accountability. It also covers additional measures related to AI deployment and oversight to help ensure safer and more responsible use of these systems.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is a proposed piece of legislation aimed at guiding the use and integration of artificial intelligence technologies in schools. It seeks to promote teacher training, ensure student data privacy, and establish clear policies for AI tools in educational settings.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students and teachers with the skills and knowledge needed to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It focuses on integrating AI education into school curricula, providing resources, and ensuring schools are prepared for the growing role of AI in education and society.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes rules to protect kids who play with AI-powered toys. It requires manufacturers to ensure these toys are safe, transparent, and age‑appropriate, and it sets up oversight to enforce compliance.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives is expressing that any American or community affected by the building or running of an AI data center deserves the right to know what’s happening and to have a say in local decisions. This stance underscores a commitment to transparency and local control over AI infrastructure developments.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would prohibit the construction and operation of AI data centers on U.S. federal lands. It aims to protect federal property and the environment by preventing large, energy‑intensive data facilities from being built on these lands.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: This act proposes new rules to guide how artificial intelligence is used in programs and services for U.S. veterans, ensuring the technology is safe, effective, and respects privacy. It requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to assess AI impacts, set up safeguards, and involve veteran communities in oversight.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to protect people from harmful or misleading content produced by AI. It requires AI developers and operators to implement safeguards and oversight to prevent the creation or spread of fabricated stories that could exploit or harm individuals or groups.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 sets out rules for using artificial intelligence in the judicial system. It requires ongoing research and monitoring to make sure AI tools are accurate, transparent, and fair in court proceedings.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill would require the government to produce a report on how artificial intelligence is used to access unminimized data collected under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. It also includes additional provisions for transparency and oversight of AI use in intelligence gathering.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 is a law designed to stop companies from using AI algorithms to secretly coordinate pricing or market behavior. It sets rules and penalties to promote fair competition and protect consumers from hidden collusion.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025 aims to reduce the U.S.'s reliance on Chinese AI technology and expertise. It proposes measures to limit imports, partnerships, and investments in Chinese AI companies, while encouraging domestic innovation and safeguarding national security.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act likely aims to broaden the use and accessibility of AI‑generated voice technology, encouraging innovation and diversity in how voices are created and deployed. It may set guidelines for ethical and responsible use, ensuring these voices are accurate, inclusive, and protect user privacy.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a legislative initiative designed to regulate the development, deployment, and oversight of artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to promote safety, ethical standards, and transparency in AI systems while ensuring accountability for their use.

title: LEARN AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
summary: The LEARN AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to set clear safety, transparency, and accountability standards for the creation and use of artificial intelligence. It aims to protect users and encourage responsible AI research by requiring developers to comply with regulatory guidelines, conduct impact assessments, and address potential misuse of AI technologies.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act aims to protect children and young people from privacy violations caused by AI technologies. It establishes guidelines for data collection, storage, and usage involving youth, ensuring transparency, consent, and strict safeguards.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: This act establishes a comprehensive framework for integrating AI education into K–12 curricula to build digital literacy and future readiness. It mandates teacher training, resource allocation, and assessment standards so that students are equipped to responsibly use and create AI technologies.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 aims to promote the study and responsible use of artificial intelligence through funding, curriculum development, and research initiatives. It seeks to strengthen AI literacy across K‑12 and higher education, ensuring that students and educators receive up‑to‑date training and resources.
